title: Tenant-aware KV residency prioritization: experimental design and instrumentation for GPU paging
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Background: As we run mixed-tenant workloads on Dedicated and Hosted modes, hotset residency pressure on GPUs leads to noisy eviction behavior: tenants with sporadic long-context requests cause page churn that degrades tail latency for others. This ticket outlines an experiment and prototype to implement tenant-aware residency prioritization for our paged/blocked KV cache so that eviction decisions and prefetch heuristics account for tenant SLAs, batch alignment, and observed token affinity.

Goals:
- Reduce cross-tenant tail-latency regressions under memory pressure.
- Improve useful-residency (fraction of prefetched pages that are actually reused) for high-priority tenants.
- Provide tooling/metrics to validate residency policies and drive rollout decisions.

Scope: Prototype runtime changes and runtime instrumentation only. No customer-facing API changes. Will include: (1) residency score calculation per KV block that includes tenant weight, recent reuse rate, and batch-affinity; (2) soft residency quotas per-tenant with adjustable decay; (3) admission controller that prefers admitting pages expected to be reused within batching windows; (4) lightweight checkpointed metadata to accelerate page rehydration for recently evicted blocks.

Design summary:
1) Residency scoring: compute score = alpha * tenant_weight + beta * reuse_rate + gamma * batch_affinity - delta * staleness_penalty. Tenant_weight comes from SLA tier mapping (hosted free vs enterprise reserved). Reuse_rate is an exponential-moving-average of accesses to the block. Batch_affinity estimates probability block will be used within the next batching horizon based on token-affinity and recent sequence-length histograms. Staleness_penalty increases with time since last access.

2) Soft quotas: allocate a dynamic "soft budget" of resident bytes per-tenant proportional to active connections and tenant_weight. Budgets float on overload with borrowing rules: high-priority tenants can preempt low-priority budgets when eviction pressure is severe. Borrowing reverses via gradual decay to avoid oscillation.

3) Admission controller: when a new block is paged in, check score threshold that scales with global load and per-tenant quota delta. Blocks below threshold are admitted to host staging only (fast-path fallback to host memory) and only promoted when reuse evidence arrives.

4) Checkpointed metadata: store compact block descriptors (page footprint, last access vector, token-affinity fingerprint) in host-side checkpoint to allow quicker rehydration without full-host->GPU binary reads for blocks that were recently evicted. This reduces page-in latency for the common case of hot-but-timed-out blocks.

Instrumentation and observability: Add the following metrics (tagged by tenant, model, and route):
- kv_page_in_latency_ms_p50/p95/p99 (per-tenant)
- kv_eviction_rate_per_min (per-tenant)
- kv_reuse_hit_ratio (resident hits / total admits)
- residency_budget_utilization_pct (per-tenant)
- page_promotion_count (host->gpu promotes triggered by reuse)
- admission_reject_rate (per-tenant)
Add traces for slow page-in paths and a dashboard comparing tail latency vs eviction_rate across tenants.

Acceptance criteria:
- Prototype compiles and runs in local dev harness (GPU emulation) and on a canary host.
- Measured improvement: reduce 99th latency due to page-in events by at least 20% for enterprise-tier tenants under synthetic cross-tenant churn workload.
- Reuse-hit-ratio improves by >= 15% for prioritized tenants without >5% regression for non-prioritized tenants.
- Dashboard surfaces new metrics and automated alert on eviction_rate > threshold.

Rollout plan:
- Phase 1: Lab prototype and microbenchmarks (this ticket).
- Phase 2: Canary on internal dogfood cluster with tenant-weight toggles.
- Phase 3: Gradual rollout with percentage traffic gating and automatic fallback to current eviction policy on regressions.

Risks & tradeoffs:
- Policy complexity: adding per-tenant budgets increases state and bookkeeping cost; mitigate by using coarse-grained bucketization (4 priority buckets).
- Fairness: aggressive prioritization could starve best-effort tenants; soft quotas and decay mitigate long-term starvation but need testing.
- Storage overhead: checkpointed metadata consumes host RAM; estimate: 0.5-2% of total KV footprint.

Dependencies: kernel allocator hooks (atomic reservation checks), runtime metrics push (traces), new dashboard panels in Console. See dependencies list.
acceptance_criteria: Prototype runs in dev harness and on canary hosts
99th percentile page-in latency reduced by >=20% for prioritized tenants under churn workload
Reuse hit ratio improved >=15% for prioritized tenants without >5% regressions for others
New metrics dashboard and eviction alert created
technical_notes: Reuse_rate EMA tau tuned to 30s in initial experiments; will iterate based on real traffic patterns
Batch_affinity uses last-2-minute sequence length distribution to predict near-term reuse windows
Checkpoint descriptor is compact (16 bytes per block) and stored in a memory-mapped file per-node for fast lookup
Admission threshold is adaptive: base threshold + load_multiplier * global_eviction_pressure
